chapters.name: Computer System (Hardware and Software)
chapters.introduction: A computer system consists of hardware (physical components) and software (programs/instructions). Covers CPU, memory, storage, I/O devices, and software types.
chapters.whyItMatters: 15-20 marks. Definitions, types, and functions of hardware/software are standard questions.

topics.name: Input and Output Devices
topics.explanation: Input devices send data to the CPU: keyboard, mouse, scanner, microphone, camera, barcode reader. Output devices receive processed data from CPU: monitor, printer, speaker, projector. I/O devices: touchscreen, modem, network card.
topics.examTip: Give 3 examples each for input and output — 1 mark per correct example.

topics.name: Memory Types
topics.explanation: Primary Memory: RAM (volatile, main working memory), ROM (non-volatile, stores BIOS). Secondary Memory: HDD, SSD, USB, CD/DVD (permanent storage). Cache memory speeds up CPU operations. Registers are fastest, smallest memory inside CPU.
topics.examTip: Know the memory hierarchy: Registers > Cache > RAM > HDD (speed order).
topics.formula:
1 Byte = 8 bits
1 KB = 1024 Bytes
1 MB = 1024 KB
1 GB = 1024 MB

chapters.name: Operating System and Application Software
chapters.introduction: Software is classified as system software (OS, utilities) and application software (word processors, browsers). Covers Windows, Linux, and common applications.
chapters.whyItMatters: 10-12 marks. OS functions and software classification are direct questions.

topics.name: Operating System Functions
topics.explanation: An OS manages hardware and software resources. Major functions: Process management, Memory management, File system management, Device management, User interface. Popular OS: Windows, macOS, Linux (Ubuntu), Android, iOS.
keyPoints: OS = interface between user and hardware
topics.examTip: List at least 5 functions of an OS with brief explanation.

chapters.name: Programming Basics and QBASIC
chapters.introduction: Programming involves writing step-by-step instructions for computers. SEE covers algorithm, flowchart, and QBASIC programming with variables, loops, conditions, and subroutines.
chapters.whyItMatters: 20-25 marks. QBASIC programs are compulsory in SEE. Flowchart questions appear every year.

topics.name: Algorithm and Flowchart
topics.explanation: Algorithm: Step-by-step logical process to solve a problem. Flowchart: Visual representation using standardised symbols — Terminal (oval), Process (rectangle), Decision (diamond), I/O (parallelogram), Connector (circle), Arrow (flow line).
keyPoints: Algorithm must be finite, definite, and effective
Oval: Start/End; Rectangle: Process; Diamond: Decision
Flowchart must have exactly ONE start and ONE end
topics.examTip: Always use correct shapes in flowcharts — wrong shapes lose marks even if logic is correct.

topics.name: QBASIC Programming
topics.explanation: QBASIC is an interpreted BASIC language. Key commands: PRINT (output), INPUT (input), LET (assignment), IF-THEN-ELSE (decision), FOR-NEXT (fixed loop), DO-LOOP (condition loop), SUB (subroutine), FUNCTION (return value). String variables end with $.
keyPoints: IF condition THEN ... ELSE ... END IF
topics.examTip: Test every QBASIC program mentally with a sample input. Wrong output = 0 marks.

  'statements

chapters.name: Networking and Cyber Security
chapters.introduction: Computer networks, internet protocols, cybersecurity threats, and digital safety practices.
chapters.whyItMatters: 15-18 marks. Networking types, protocols, and cybersecurity are topical and appear regularly.

topics.name: Networking Basics
topics.explanation: LAN (Local Area Network): within a building. MAN (Metropolitan): city-wide. WAN (Wide Area Network): nationwide/worldwide. Internet = global WAN. Protocols: TCP/IP (data transmission), HTTP (web), FTP (file transfer), SMTP (email), DNS (domain name). IP address identifies devices.
keyPoints: HTTP: web browsing; FTP: file transfer
IP Address: unique identifier for device on network
topics.examTip: Know full forms of all protocols and network types — common fill-in-the-blank questions.

topics.name: Cyber Security
topics.explanation: Cybersecurity protects computers and networks from digital attacks. Common threats: viruses, worms, trojans, ransomware, phishing, hacking. Preventions: antivirus, firewall, strong passwords, 2FA, regular updates, VPN. Nepal's Electronic Transaction Act 2063 B.S. governs cyber crimes.
keyPoints: Virus: self-replicating; Ransomware: encrypts then demands payment
Electronic Transaction Act 2063 BS — Nepal's cyber law
topics.examTip: List at least 3 cyber crimes and 3 preventive measures for full marks.
